root_cause.text: The X.509 extension parser in `crypto/asymmetric_keys/x509_cert_parser.c` dereferenced `v[0]` for Basic Constraints and Key Usage before verifying that `vlen` was large enough, allowing an out-of-bounds read on empty extensions.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the length checks ahead of the first-byte checks in `x509_process_extension()`—for Key Usage it changes from `if (v[0] != ASN1_BTS) ... if (vlen < 4)` to `if (vlen < 4) ... if (v[0] != ASN1_BTS)`, and for Basic Constraints from `if (v[0] != (ASN1_CONS_BIT | ASN1_SEQ)) ... if (vlen < 2)` to `if (vlen < 2) ... if (v[0] != (ASN1_CONS_BIT | ASN1_SEQ))`—matching the CVE description that an empty extension caused the first byte to be read before length validation.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch moves the length checks ahead of the first-byte checks in `x509_process_extension()`—for Key Usage it changes from `if (v[0] != ASN1_BTS) ... if (vlen < 4)` to `if (vlen < 4) ... if (v[0] != ASN1_BTS)`, and for Basic Constraints from `if (v[0] != (ASN1_CONS_BIT | ASN1_SEQ)) ... if (vlen < 2)` to `if (vlen < 2) ... if (v[0] != (ASN1_CONS_BIT | ASN1_SEQ))`—matching the CVE description that an empty extension caused the first byte to be read before length validation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder X.509 extension validation checks to avoid accessing the buffer before confirming its minimum length.
intent_record.what: The order of two validation checks was changed in x509_process_extension(): the function now checks whether vlen is at least 4 before verifying that v[0] equals ASN1_BTS, whereas previously the ASN1_BTS type check came first.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this reordering prevents the code from reading v[0] before confirming that the buffer is long enough, avoiding an out-of-bounds access when the extension value is shorter than 4 bytes. The functional validation logic remains the same, but it is now performed in a safer order.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder X.509 extension validation to avoid reading past the buffer on short malformed inputs.
intent_record.what: In x509_process_extension(), the order of two validation checks was changed: the code now checks `if (vlen < 2) return -EBADMSG;` before verifying `v[0] == (ASN1_CONS_BIT | ASN1_SEQ)`, whereas previously the tag check came first.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from reading `v[0]` when the extension value length is smaller than 2 bytes, avoiding an out-of-bounds access on malformed input while preserving the same validation outcome for valid data.
